top_signals.title: The Hidden $40-Per-Barrel Cost Driving Oil Prices Higher
top_signals.summary: When Americans think about the price of oil, they usually focus on the number quoted every day in financial markets. If Brent crude is trading above $100 a barrel or West Texas Intermediate is near $100, those numbers become shorthand for whether oil is expensive or cheap. But that market price is only part of what ultimately determines the cost of getting crude oil to a refinery. But transportation has become a cost that has become impossible to ignore.
